questions.text:
Each of the following sentences has a blank space and five words are given below. Click on the word which you consider the most APPROPRIATE to fit the blank.

We have to raise some money to _____ this garden.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'beautify'.
 
Key Points
  • The word "beautify" means to make something more attractive or pleasant. (सुंदर बनाना)
  • In the given context, raising money to improve the garden suggests making it more beautiful.
  • The other options: "pacify," "clarify," "inhibit," and "analyze" do not fit the context appropriately.

​Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 3'.

Complete Sentence: We have to raise some money to beautify this garden.

Additional Information
  • Pacify (शांत करना): means to calm or soothe.
  • Clarify (स्पष्ट करना): means to make something clear or understandable.
  • Inhibit (रोकना): means to restrain or prevent.
  • Analyze (विश्लेषण करना): means to study or examine something in detail.

questions.text:
In the following sentence, some parts have errors and some are correct. Find out which part has an error and mark it as your answer. If there is no error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Everyone of us must have (A) experienced how people (B)/ have to put up on a good (C)/ deal of discomfort while travelling. (D)/ No error (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 3.
Key Points
  • The error lies in part C of the sentence.
  • The phrasal verb "put up on" is used incorrectly.
  • The correct idiomatic expression is "put up with," which means to tolerate or endure something unpleasant or difficult.
  • Replacing "on" with "with" makes the sentence grammatically sound.
Therefore, the correct answer is C.
Correct Sentence: "Everyone of us must have experienced how people have to put up with a good deal of discomfort while travelling."
Additional Information
  • A: "Everyone of us must have" – This part is correct; "must have" is used for a strong probability or certainty about the past.
  • B: "experienced how people" – This part is correct; "experienced" is the past participle required after "have."
  • D: "deal of discomfort while travelling." – This part is correct; "a good deal of" is a common quantifier for uncountable nouns.
  • No error – This option is incorrect because a grammatical error exists in the usage of the phrasal verb.

questions.text:
Read the sentence to find out whether there is an error in it. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. The number of that part is the answer. If there is no error, the answer is (5). Ignore errors of punctuation, if any

 It is a known fact (1) that the problem (2) is between I and her (3) and we better be able to solve it soon (4) No error (5)

options.text: and we better be able to solve it soon

questions.explanation:
The correct option is 3) i.e is between I and her

  • The error is in part 3 of the sentence
  • The pronouns should be 'me' instead of 'I'  after the preposition.
  • The pronoun must be objective in nature after the preposition.

  • The subjective pronoun (they, she etc) cannot be placed after the preposition.
    • My sister send it to they  ​
  • The objective pronoun (them, her) must be placed after the preposition
    • My sister send it to them 
  • Objective pronoun is placed after the verb and acts as the object in the sentence.
    • The cake was baked by her. 

In most cases, the pronoun is placed after the preposition and one sentence might have two such situations. 

The correct sentence is: It is a known fact that the problem is between me and her and we better be able to solve it soon.

Read the sentence to find out whether there is an error in it. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. The number of that part is the answer. If there is no error, the answer is (5). Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.

Mrs Margaret (1) has been working (2) in our office as an assistant (3) from 25 years (4) No error (5)

options.text: in our office as an assistant

questions.explanation:
The correct option is 4) i.e from 25 years.

  • The error is in part 4 of the sentence
  • The preposition should be 'for' instead of 'from'.
  • The tense used in the sentence talks about an action which has been continuing for a significant amount of time.
  • The preposition 'for' is used to denote a specific duration in the sentence

  • The preposition 'from' is used when the scheduled time for the action is mentioned in the sentence 
    • The meeting will be conducted from 7 am to 9 am.
    • My brother studied for two hours.
    • Our friend visited us for few minutes.
  • The preposition from is also used to denote a specific part of any journey
    • We will travel from Mumbai to Bangalore

Important Points

  • In few cases, the preposition since is used to also denote time which involves a certain point of the whole time period
    • It has been raining since yesterday.

The correct sentence is: Mrs Margaret has been working in our office as an assistant for 25 years.

In the following question, two columns are given containing three phrases each. In the first column, phrases are A, B, and C, and in the second column, the phrases are D, E and F. A phrase from the first column may or may not connect with a phrase from the second column to make a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. There are five options, four of which display the sequence(s) in which the phrases can be joined to form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence. If, none of the options given forms a correct sentence after combination, select ‘None of these’ as your answer. 

Column (1)

Column (2)

(A) War crimes had occurred 

(D) your papers.

(B)The editors do not wish to publish

(E)throughout history and continues to this day.

(C) Microplastics may pose a risk 

(F)to aquatic environments.
questions.explanation:
The correct sentences are - 

  • B-D: The editors do not wish to publish your papers.  
  • C-F: Microplastics may pose a risk to aquatic environments.

Key Points

  • We need to join each sentence part given in column 1 to their correct counterparts given in column 2. The sentences should not only be conceptually correct but also grammatically error free. This would allow us to come at the correct solution.
    • Part B talks about something that the editors do not wish to do. As editors are people involved in publishing, parts B and D should join. So, B-D.
    • Part C talks about how a certain thing (microplastics) can pose a risk. It should join with part F  which mentions who or what is affected by this risk. So, C-F.
  • ​The correct combinations are reflected in option 3, making it the correct answer.

Important Points

  • Conceptually parts A and E can join but it would create a grammatical error. Part A uses the perfect past tense (had occurred) implying that war crimes no longer occur. But joining it with part E  would mean that thw war crimes have continued occurring in present time too, in which case the present continuous tense (have occurred) should be used.

Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence has an error. Read the sentence to find the error and mark the corresponding option. If the sentence has no error, choose option 5 'No error’ as your answer.

She don't have (A)/ any idea about (B)/ the changes that (C)/ were implemented. (D)/ No Error (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'don't have' (A).

 Key Points

  • The problem lies with the usage of 'don't' with a singular noun ‘She’.
  • The contraction 'don't' is used with plural subjects, while 'doesn't' is used with singular subjects.
  • Therefore, 'don't have' should be replaced by 'doesn't have' in sentence A.
  • Rest of the sentence follows the principles of English grammar and does not possess any error.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 Additional Information

  • Remember the correct agreement between subject and verb is a fundamental rule in English grammar. "Doesn't" should be used with singular subjects and "don't" with plural ones.

questions.text:
Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence has an error. Read the sentence to find the error and mark the corresponding option. If the sentence has no error, choose option 5 'No error’ as your answer.

He had (A)/ an unique (B)/ idea that made (C)/ him successful. (D)/ No Error (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'an unique' (B).

 Key Points

  • The error in sentence B is a common one. The indefinite article 'an' is used before words that start with vowel sounds.
  • However, 'unique' starts with a 'y' sound, which is a semivowel. Hence, the correct article to use is 'a'.
  • Therefore, 'an unique' should be corrected as 'a unique'.
  • The rest of the sentence is grammatically correct, adhering to language rules.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 Additional Information

  • Keep in mind, 'a' is used before words that begin with a consonant sound, and 'an' is used before words that begin with a vowel sound.

Direction: In the following question, one part of the sentence has an error. Read the sentence to find the error and mark the corresponding option. If the sentence has no error, choose option 5 'No error’ as your answer.

She try to (A)/ balance her (B)/ professional life with (C)/ her personal responsibilities.(D)/ No Error (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'try’ (A).


Key Points

  • Sentence A contains a subject-verb agreement error; 'She' being a singular subject, requires 'tries' instead of 'try'.
  • As per the rules of English grammar, add -es or -s for the third person singular in the present tense.
  • So, the corrected option would be 'tries' instead of 'try'.
  • Other parts of the sentence do not contain any grammatical errors.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 Additional Information

  • Making sure your verbs agree with your subjects (singular subject needs singular verb, plural subject needs plural verb) is essential for correct English.

questions.text:
Directions: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the button corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the ''No error'' option.

The thieves (A)/ cleaned out (B)/ the shop in (C)/ a hour (D)/. No error /(E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'D' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • In the fourth part of the given sentence, the use of the article 'a' before the noun 'hour' is incorrect.
  • In the given sentence, the noun 'hour' is not a specified noun.
    • 'A' and 'an' are indefinite articles, which means that they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.
      • We use 'a' before a consonant sound, and we use 'an' before a vowel sound (here, hour).
    • The definite article 'the' is used before singular and plural nouns when the noun is specific or particular.
    • ''No article'' is used when we refer to general ideas, plurals, or uncountable nouns.
  • Therefore, the article 'an' should be used in place of the article 'a'.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: The thieves cleaned out the shop in an hour.

Additional Information

  • There are three articles: a, an, and the. Articles are used before nouns or noun equivalents and are a type of adjective.
     
                       RULES       COUNT NOUNS NON-COUNT NOUNS
    Specific identity not known a, an (no article)
    Specific identity is known the the
    All things or things in general (no article) (no article)

questions.text:
Direction: Evaluate the following word, accompanied by three sentences containing it. Determine the sentence(s) that accurately convey the meaning of the given word.

SURREAL

A. His writing style is quite surreal, filled with intricate metaphors and deep philosophical themes.
B. Social media influencers have the power to make products go surreal with their endorsements.
C. The surreal melodies of the flute echoed through the forest, creating a sense of tranquillity and serenity.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 5.


Key Points

  • To answer this question, let's first understand the meaning of the given word - 
  • Surreal - (Adjective) - having the qualities of surrealism; bizarre (अवास्तविक)
    • For Example - 
    • Hearing the news of my promotion at work was such a surreal and exciting surprise.
  • After understanding the meaning of the given word i.e. surreal, we can conclude that all the given sentences are incorrect.
  • Sentence A - His writing style is quite surreal, filled with intricate metaphors and deep philosophical themes.
    • This sentence is incorrect because "surreal" implies a dreamlike or unreal quality, while "cerebral or intellectual" better suits the description of intricate metaphors and deep philosophical themes.
  • Sentence B - Social media influencers have the power to make products go surreal with their endorsements.
    • This sentence is incorrect because "surreal" is not the right word here. "Surreal" means bizarre or dreamlike, while the context requires "viral," which means widely shared or popular.
  • Sentence C - The surreal melodies of the flute echoed through the forest, creating a sense of tranquillity and serenity.
    • This sentence is incorrect because "surreal" suggests a dreamlike or bizarre quality, which doesn't fit the serene and peaceful atmosphere. "Ethereal or elegant" is more appropriate, conveying a delicate and otherworldly feeling.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is "None of these."

questions.text:
Directions: Given below is a word, followed by three sentences that consist of that word. Identify the sentence(s) that best express(es) the meaning of the word. Choose option 5 'None of the above' if the word is not suitable in any of the sentences.

IMPERATIVE

A. The school district’s new policy makes it imperative for every child to be familiar with the escape routes on school buses.

B. I became angry when the customer service agent kept giving me imperative solutions to my computer problems.

C. Although she thought she was just being funny, her teacher didn’t agree and sent her to the principal’s office for being imperative.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Only A.'

Key Points

  • The given word 'Imperative' means very important or urgent. (बहुत महत्वपूर्ण या आवश्‍यक; अत्‍यावश्‍यक)
  • Let us explore the given sentences:
    • The word 'imperative' is used correctly in the first sentence as it talks about a policy that makes it very important for every child to be familiar with the escape routes on school buses.
      • Example: It's imperative that you see a doctor immediately.
    • The word 'irrelevant' should be used in the second sentence as it talks about the customer service agent who kept giving unimportant or insignificant solutions to the computer problems.
      • The word 'irrelevant' means not connected with something or important to it. (किसी वस्‍तु से असंबद्घ या उसके लिए महत्वहीन, अप्रासंगिक, असंबद्घ)
    • The word 'impertinent' should be used in the third sentence as it talks about a teacher sending a student to the principal’s office for being disrespectful.
      • The word 'impertinent' means not showing respect to somebody who is older and more important; rude. (स्‍वयं से अधिक महत्वपूर्ण एवं ज्‍येष्‍ठ व्‍यक्ति का सम्‍मान न करते हुए)
  • Therefore, only sentence A best expresses the meaning of the given word.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Sentence A: The school district’s new policy makes it imperative for every child to be familiar with the escape routes on school buses.

Sentence B: I became angry when the customer service agent kept giving me irrelevant solutions to my computer problems.

Sentence C: Although she thought she was just being funny, her teacher didn’t agree and sent her to the principal’s office for being impertinent.

questions.text:
Directions: Given below is a word, followed by three sentences that consist of that word. Identify the sentence(s) that best express(es) the meaning of the word. Choose option 5 'None of the above' if the word is not suitable in any of the sentences.

FLOUT

A. When the nurse failed to flout the procedures for issuing medication, patients became ill and threatened to sue the hospital.

B. People find themselves in trouble because they think they’re clever enough to flout the law without getting caught.

C. Safety guidelines exist for a reason, and if you flout them, there could be serious consequences.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Both B and C.'

Key Points

  • The given word 'Flout' means to openly disregard a rule, law, or convention. (क़ानून, नियम आदि अवहेलना करना, न मानना, उल्‍लंघन करना)
  • Let us explore the given sentences:
    • The word 'obey' should be used in the first sentence as it talks about the patients who became ill as the nurse failed to carry out or follow the procedures for issuing medication.
      • The word 'obey' means to do what you are told to do. (आज्ञा का पालन करना)
    • The word 'flout' is used correctly in the second sentence as it talks about those people who think they’re clever enough to break the law without getting caught.
      • Example: Many motorcyclists flout the law by not wearing helmets.
    • The word 'flout' is used correctly in the third sentence as it talks about the serious consequences of refusing to obey safety guidelines.
      • Example: No one can flout the law with impunity.
  • Therefore, both B and C best express the meaning of the given word.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Sentence A: When the nurse failed to obey the procedures for issuing medication, patients became ill and threatened to sue the hospital.

Sentence B: People find themselves in trouble because they think they’re clever enough to flout the law without getting caught.

Sentence C: Safety guidelines exist for a reason, and if you flout them, there could be serious consequences.

questions.text:
In each question, one sentence is given in which certain words are in bold and numbered from A to E. Below the sentence are given five options with possible pairs of interchange of those bold words. Choose the pair(s) of words which are needed to be interchanged to make the sentence grammatically correct and meaningful.

75% of according(A)entrepreneurs experience (B)personal financial hardship,  social (C)to a 2019 study by(D) World Economic Forum. (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Option 2'.

Key Points

  • The word "according" (A) is incorrectly placed. It is used to present the source of information and should be swapped with "to" (C) to make the sentence grammatically correct.
  • The correct sentence structure requires "according to" (A-C) to attribute the information to the World Economic Forum study.
  • Thus, "according" and "to" need to be interchanged to make the sentence coherent and meaningful.

Hence, the correct answer is 'A - C'.

Correct Sentence: 75% of entrepreneurs experience personal financial hardship, according to a 2019 study by World Economic Forum.

Additional Information

  • Option 1: Interchanging "according" (A) and "World Economic Forum" (E) disrupts the sentence structure and does not make sense.
  • Option 3: Interchanging "study by" (D) and "World Economic Forum" (E) results in a grammatically incorrect sentence.
  • Option 4: Interchanging "experience" (B) and "study by" (D) disrupts the meaning of the sentence.
  • Option 5: No interchange required is incorrect because the phrase "according to" (A-C) is not correctly placed in the sentence.

questions.text: Which title and summary, respectively, best encapsulate the passage's essence?

options.text: "Ethics in Flux: Balancing Values in Contemporary Society," Addressing contemporary dilemmas, the passage underscores the decline of ethics, advocating for early education's pivotal role in nurturing moral consciousness.

"Moral Education: Cultivating Integrity Amidst Modern Chaos," The passage delves into modern ethical dilemmas, advocating for early value education to counteract growing societal transgressions and cultivate principled citizens.

"Upholding Moral Values: Nurturing Integrity in a Fast-Paced World," The passage highlights the erosion of moral values in a fast-paced world and emphasizes the crucial role of education in nurturing integrity and ethical behaviour from a young age.

"Guiding Principles: Building Character Amid Life's Rush," Analyzing societal trends, the passage scrutinizes moral decline, emphasizing education's critical role in shaping ethical foundations amid today's complexities.

"Values Beyond Time: Sustaining Morality Amidst Urban Turmoil," The passage explores the fading ethical landscape, emphasizing the importance of instilling moral principles early to guide individuals toward integrity and societal betterment.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 3.

Key Points

  • To answer this question, first read the passage carefully to understand what the passage is about.
  • Summary of the passage:
  • The passage reflects on the fading moral compass in today's fast-paced world, emphasizing the need to instil values like empathy and honesty early on. It highlights how education, guided by moral principles, shapes individuals of integrity, aiming to combat societal ethical decline and nurture a principled generation for a better society.
  • Now, Let's analyze the options:
  • Option 1 - "Ethics in Flux: Balancing Values in Contemporary Society," Addressing contemporary dilemmas, the passage underscores the decline of ethics, advocating for early education's pivotal role in nurturing moral consciousness.
    • This option captures the discussion on the decline of ethics but lacks emphasis on the essential role of education in fostering moral values from an early age. It doesn't fully encapsulate the passage's emphasis on education's significance in shaping ethical behaviour in children.
    • So, this cannot be the answer.
  • Option 2 - "Moral Education: Cultivating Integrity Amidst Modern Chaos," The passage delves into modern ethical dilemmas, advocating for early value education to counteract growing societal transgressions and cultivate principled citizens.
    • This option centres on moral education and societal dilemmas but doesn't explicitly highlight the erosion of moral values or stress the critical role of education in addressing these issues. It fails to encompass the passage's comprehensive emphasis on the decline of moral values and the pivotal role of education in countering it.
    • So, this cannot be the answer.
  • Option 3 - "Upholding Moral Values: Nurturing Integrity in a Fast-Paced World," The passage highlights the erosion of moral values in a fast-paced world and emphasizes the crucial role of education in nurturing integrity and ethical behaviour from a young age.
    • This option succinctly encapsulates the core essence of the passage by acknowledging the decline of moral values in today's fast-paced world and stressing the pivotal role of education in nurturing ethical behaviour from an early age. It accurately reflects the passage's emphasis on the erosion of values and the significance of education in addressing this issue, making it the most fitting title and summary.
    • So, this is the correct answer.
  • Option 4 - "Guiding Principles: Building Character Amid Life's Rush," Analyzing societal trends, the passage scrutinizes moral decline, emphasizing education's critical role in shaping ethical foundations amid today's complexities.
    • While this option discusses moral decline and acknowledges education's importance, it lacks specificity in addressing the erosion of moral values and doesn't emphasize early education's role, which is pivotal in the passage's essence.
    • So, this cannot be the answer.
  • Option 5 - "Values Beyond Time: Sustaining Morality Amidst Urban Turmoil," The passage explores the fading ethical landscape, emphasizing the importance of instilling moral principles early to guide individuals toward integrity and societal betterment.
    • Although this option mentions the fading ethical landscape and stresses the importance of instilling moral principles early, it doesn't comprehensively cover the passage's emphasis on the erosion of values in today's fast-paced world and the responsibility of education in combating this decline.
    • So, this cannot be the answer.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is "Upholding Moral Values: Nurturing Integrity in a Fast-Paced World," The passage highlights the erosion of moral values in a fast-paced world and emphasizes the crucial role of education in nurturing integrity and ethical behaviour from a young age.

questions.text: How does the passage suggest teachers could evaluate students' commitment to moral principles?

options.text: Seamlessly integrating values into the curriculum

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2.

Key Points

  • To answer this question, let's focus on the information provided in the passage regarding evaluating students' commitment to moral principles. 
  • The passage mentions, "To gauge their understanding and commitment to these values, teachers may also consider conducting unmonitored class tests." This specific mention of "unmonitored class tests" implies a method where students are evaluated on their adherence to moral principles without direct supervision. 
  • The passage further elaborates that such exercises instil the belief that upholding moral principles is a personal responsibility, even without oversight. This approach aims to make these principles second nature to individuals, fostering integrity. 
  • Therefore, the correct answer is "Through unmonitored class tests."

questions.text:
Which of the following sentence(s) can be inferred from the given passage?

A. The decline in societal empathy and the proliferation of misconduct signal the erosion of foundational values in today’s culture.
B. In a world devoid of material pursuits, societal progress is hindered by an overwhelming emphasis on communal ethical codes.
C. The ethical compass, once the cornerstone of societal integrity, seems overshadowed by the relentless pursuit of individual goals.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 3.

Key Points

  • To answer this question, let's analyze the given sentences:
  • Sentence A - "The decline in societal empathy and the proliferation of misconduct signal the erosion of foundational values in today’s culture."
    • This sentence aligns with the passage's discussion on the erosion of moral values leading to unethical behaviour, indicating a decline in societal empathy and an increase in misconduct.
  • Sentence B - "In a world devoid of material pursuits, societal progress is hindered by an overwhelming emphasis on communal ethical codes."
    • This sentence cannot be inferred from the passage. The passage primarily discusses the erosion of moral values in a fast-paced, self-centered world, rather than a world devoid of material pursuits. It focuses on individual pursuits taking precedence over communal ethical codes, not their absence hindering societal progress.
  • Sentence C - "The ethical compass, once the cornerstone of societal integrity, seems overshadowed by the relentless pursuit of individual goals."
    • This sentence resonates with the passage's theme, highlighting how the pursuit of individual goals has overshadowed the importance of ethical principles that were once fundamental to societal integrity.
  • So, out of the three sentences given, both A and C can be inferred from the passage, while sentence B cannot be inferred. 
  • Therefore, the correct answer is "Both A & C."

questions.text: Which pair of words represents the synonym and antonym, respectively, for the word "precedence" in the context of the passage?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2.

Key Points

  • To answer this question, let's first understand the meaning of the word, "precedence," given in the question:
  • Precedence - priority or greater importance given to something over other matters; the condition of being considered more important than something else (पूर्वाधिकार)
  • For Example -
  • The safety of the passengers takes precedence over all other concerns for the airline crew during flights.
  • The word "precedence" in the context of the passage refers to the priority or superiority given to individual pursuits over other things. Therefore, we are looking for a pair of words that represent a synonym and an antonym for "precedence" in this context.

 

  • Now, let's consider the options:
  • Option 1 - "Scrutinize, Disregard"
  • Scrutinize - to examine or inspect closely and thoroughly (जांचना)
    • For Example -
    • Before finalizing the contract, the legal team will scrutinize every clause to ensure accuracy and legality.
  • Disregard - to pay no attention to; ignore or treat as unworthy of consideration (अनदेखा करना)
    • For Example -
    • Despite numerous warnings, he chose to disregard the safety protocols, putting himself at risk.
  • Here, "Scrutinize" means to examine closely, which doesn’t align with the meaning of "precedence." "Disregard" means to ignore or pay no attention, which is an antonym but not the one that fits here.
    • So, this can not be the answer.
  • Option 2 - "Ascendancy, Inconsequence"
  • Ascendancy - a position of dominant power or influence, often gained gradually or through superiority in a particular field or aspect (अधिकार)
    • For Example -
    • Her expertise and experience in the field gave her an ascendancy over her colleagues, making her the go-to person for advice and guidance.
  • Inconsequence - the lack of importance, significance, or relevance; something lacking in consequence or importance (अप्रासंगिकता)
    • For Example -
    • His arguments held no weight due to their inconsequence in the context of the discussion, and they were swiftly dismissed by the panel.
  • Here, "Ascendancy" means dominance or a position of power, which aligns with the concept of "precedence." "Inconsequence" means lack of importance or significance, serving as the antonym that fits the context.
    • So, this is the correct answer.
  • Option 3 - "Amalgamation, Separation"
  • Amalgamation - the action, process, or result of combining or uniting multiple entities into one, often creating a whole that is more complex or comprehensive (संघटन)
    • For Example -
    • The amalgamation of different departments within the company aimed to streamline operations and enhance efficiency by merging their functions.
  • Separation - the act or process of setting or keeping apart; the state of being apart or detached from others (विभाजन)
    • For Example -
    • The separation of powers within the government ensures a system of checks and balances where each branch has distinct functions and responsibilities.
  • Here, "Amalgamation" means the merging or combining of things, which doesn't relate to "precedence." "Separation" means to divide or detach, also not fitting the context.
    • So, this can not be the answer.
  • Option 4 - "Negligibility, Dominance"
  • Negligibility - the state or quality of being so small, unimportant, or insignificant that it's not worth considering or taking into account (तुच्छता)
    • For Example -
    • In the grand scheme of the project, the typo in the presentation had a level of negligibility that didn't affect the overall impact.
  • Dominance - the power, authority, or influence over others; the state of being in control or command (प्रमुखता)
    • For Example -
    • The company's dominance in the market allowed it to set industry standards and trends.
  • Here, "Negligibility" refers to being unimportant or insignificant, which is closer to an antonym for "precedence." "Dominance" aligns more with the synonym of "precedence."
    • So, this can not be the answer as well because it presents an atonym-synonym pair, not a synonym-antonym pair as asked in the question.
  • Option 5 - "Fortitude, Weakness"
  • Fortitude - mental and emotional strength in facing difficulty, adversity, danger, or temptation courageously (साहस, धैर्य)
    • For Example -
    • Her fortitude during the challenging times inspired everyone around her to persevere.
  • Weakness - the state or condition of lacking strength or firmness; a disadvantage or fault (कमजोरी)
    • For Example -
    • His fear of failure was his greatest weakness, hindering his progress in various aspects of life.
  • Here, "Fortitude" means courage or strength of character, not directly related to "precedence." "Weakness" serves as an antonym but is not in line with the context.
    • So, this can not be the answer.
  • Hence, among the given options, the pair that represents the synonym and antonym for "precedence" in the context of the passage is option 2: Ascendancy (synonym) and Inconsequence (antonym).
  • Therefore, the correct answer is "Ascendancy, Inconsequence."

Directions: Pick out the most effective form of the word from the given options to fill in the blanks to make the sentence meaningfully complete.

Unemployment rate _______ in the US as govt stimulus for recovery _______.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. rises, fades​​.

Key Points

  • From the context of the sentence, the verbs should be used in the given blanks.
  • Let us explore the options:
    • The first option is correct as the tense (simple present tense) of both the words are correct and also their meaning fits into the sentence. Also, the plural subject "unemployment rate" takes the plural verb 'rises'.
    • The second option is incorrect as 'rise' is the singular form of the verb and "unemployment rate" is a plural subject and 'faded' is the past tense of the verb.
    • The third option is incorrect as 'rose' is the past tense of the verb 'rise' and 'fading' is the present participle form of 'fade'.
    • The fourth option is incorrect as 'faded' is the past tense of the verb. 'Rises' is still okay for the first blank but 'faded' is not fit for the second blank.
    • The fifth option is incorrect as 'risen' is the past participle of the verb. 'Fades' is still okay for the second blank but 'risen' is not fit for the first blank.
  • Hence, the correct option is "rises, fades".
     

​Complete Sentence: Unemployment rate rises in the US as govt stimulus for recovery fades.

Important Points

  • Important Tips and Tricks to solve double fillers: 
    • Do not read options: Read the sentence and think of a word that 'fits' the sentence. Now go to the options and choose the word that best replaces the word that you had thought of initially.
    • Elimination method: In certain questions, our knowledge and understanding of vocabulary and common idioms-phrases may be tested. Hence, be sure to have a good skill set of such phrases.
    • Use grammar clues: Keep a close watch at the tense of the sentence, subject-verb agreement, whether the blank in the sentence is after the article 'an' etc.
    • Use Connotation: Each word expresses two things: a definition and a connotation. A connotation is a positive, negative, or neutral feeling that is implied by or associated with a word.
    • Identify the Indicators: Indicators tell us what is coming up. They indicate if the question is moving to draw a contrast with something stated previously, or support something stated previously.
